declaration: not-null: originalName must not be null

On the upload path a null original filename is replaced with Constant.DEFAULT_FILENAME, so null never reaches persistence.
limitations: Handling classed as elegant because the rejection is an intentional, field-specific validation response; the HTTP status (500) and errorCode INTERNAL_ERROR are not ideal.;Upload-path substitution (null -> DEFAULT_FILENAME) was not exercised: a multipart part without a filename is not bound as MultipartFile.;Other transfer methods (OSS/S3/URL) use the same validator but require external services and were not exercised.

declaration: unique: username must be unique
subject: login_data(username)
rationale: Sequential duplicate registration is rejected by the application pre-check (errorCode USERNAME_EXISTS) before any INSERT. limitations: USERNAME_EXISTS is returned with HTTP status 500.;Under concurrency, enforcement is DATABASE_ENFORCED_UNHANDLED.

subject: org.eclipse.jifa.server.domain.entity.shared.file.BaseFileEntity.user
rationale: BaseFileEntity.user -> UserEntity (nullable FK user_id -> users, present in DDL for files/deleted_files/transferring_files). The user is taken from the authenticated JWT (userService.getCurrentUserRef()), so the client cannot point it at a nonexistent user; users cannot be deleted through any API. Read-back shows user_id=2 on files uploaded by the test user.

declaration: association: org.eclipse.jifa.server.domain.entity.shared.user.LoginDataEntity.user -> UserEntity
subject: org.eclipse.jifa.server.domain.entity.shared.user.LoginDataEntity.user
rationale: LoginDataEntity.user -> UserEntity (FK user_id not null unique) is always set to the user saved in the same transaction. When the login_data insert failed (U04), the whole transaction rolled back, leaving no orphan users row (read-back). Not client-controllable.
